item.title: Experimental study on swash zone transport of a coral-gravel beach
item.description: Coral reefs and rocky coasts are present around the globe. Large waves typically generated by storms are able to damage reefs and produce coralline sediments, thus acting as a sediment source on top of the reef. These reef fragments are then transported with the overlying sediments with the waves. Generally, coral sediments are of sedimentary composition e.g. limestone, giving the sediments a porous nature. This porous nature of the sediment contributes to the overall porosity of the overlying beach.
